religious leaders asked jesus was whether the israelites should or should not pay taxes to caesar (the ruler of rome who controls israel). a trick question wanting to force jesus to pick a team: was jesus cheering for rome or the israelites? read today’s gospel mt 22:15 – 21. jesus points out that caesar’s image and name are on the money and says “give to caesar what is caesar’s and give to god what is god’s.” in other words, jesus was telling the phari sees that the image they wear is the team they are on – and the image we all wear is the image of god. the pharisees tried to stop jesus because they forgot what team they were actually on. we learn from jesus what it means to be on god’s team, we learn to share with others the same love, forgiveness, and healing that jesus offered to those around him. the more we do those same things as jesus did, the more we help others know they belong to god’s team, too. dear god, thank you for jesus, who reminds us that each of us belong to you and then shows us how to share your love with others. thank you and amen family prayer time: (loyola press) as your family gathers, make a list of the activities that your family spends time doing together, such as household tasks, jobs, academics, and recreational activities. talk about the importance of each of these activities and what would happen if there were an imbalance by spending too much time on one activity at the expense of another. in today’s gospel jesus speaks of the necessity of giving things their proper importance. read matt 22:15-21. the herodians and pharisees were giving too much importance to the issue of the payment of taxes. jesus says to them that loving and honouring god is of greater importance. in family life we do many important things, but we remember that god is of the greatest importance in our lives. pray that your family will learn to keep things in proper perspective, remembering to keep god first in your l ives. pray together today’s psalm, psalm 95. mission month: world mission sunday- our mission : send me, lord, out into the world that begins at my front door. may my every word flow from your heart and my actions be of love and peace that everything i do or say reflects your great mercy to all. help me witness to your truth no l ess in my silence than in my words and show me, lord, the way i should go. help me to see that my solemn duty to spread your gospel to everyone in the world is second only to their right to hear and respond to it. open my eyes to your presence in others and my ears to recognise your voice especially in the poor and oppressed. amen. rosary for peace continues before the 11am mass on each sunday of october, beginning at 10.40am. this sunday is world mission sunday: the theme for this year’s celebration of mission sunday in christ, united in mission”. world mission sunday is the holy father’s annual appeal for spiritual and financial support so that the life-giving work of overseas mission and missionaries can continue. mission sund ay collections are held in every single parish where the church is present. it is a moment of universal solidarity when each member of t he church plays their part in supporting each other. all offerings and donations made for world mission sunday become part of the holy father’s universal solidarity fund. this fund is a lifeline for struggling missionaries and the communities they serve across africa, asia and latin america, where over 1,100 mission dioceses are found. as these dioceses form and grow, so do their needs. on top of this, mission dioceses are often in remote areas devastated by war and natural disasters, or wheres uppressed communities are just opening up to the life-sav ing message of jesus christ. this is why world mission sunday is so important. it offers young dioceses the financial and spiritual assistance they need to help their men, women, and children to survive and t hrive. to donate, use the envelope in your offertory collection box, the special envelopes available in church or donate through t he missio.ie website. straide harvest mass of thanksgiving: sincere thanks to the pastoral council and to all who helped organise, and make all the preparations for last sunday’s harvest mass. thanks also to all who p articipated – choir, the children who brought up gifts, led the prayers and served, readers and communion minister – and made it
